extraction.name: LongBench
extraction.description: A bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding comprising 21 datasets across 6 task categories in English and Chinese. It covers single-doc QA, multi-doc QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion, with all datasets standardized into a unified format for automatic evaluation of LLMs.
extraction.creator: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongBench was constructed by reusing and sampling from existing datasets (e.g., NarrativeQA, Qasper, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue, DuReader) and by manually curating new MultiFieldQA datasets from collected documents/articles across multiple sources. For MultiFieldQA, three Ph.D. students annotated question-answer pairs. For multi-document QA, complete passages and distracting passages were added and randomly ordered to create long-context inputs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw/source data included long stories, NLP papers, documents and articles from multiple sources such as legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, and academic papers, as well as Wikipedia passages and DuReader materials based on Baidu Search and Baidu Zhidao.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For the manually curated MultiFieldQA datasets, three Ph.D. students annotated a question and answer for each article, aiming for definitive answers; annotators ensured answers were inferable from the documents and that evidence placement was fairly random to avoid positional bias. The section also notes prior dataset annotation methods: Qasper was annotated by NLP practitioners, HotpotQA questions were written by native speakers given two related paragraphs, 2WikiMultihopQA questions were synthesized through manually designed templates, and MuSiQue questions were paraphrased by annotators.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three annotators per article for MultiFieldQA.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three Ph.D. students annotated MultiFieldQA; Qasper was annotated by NLP practitioners; HotpotQA questions were written by native speakers.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Random sampling and uniform sampling were used to extract benchmark data; for multi-document QA, distracting passages/documents were added and passages were randomly ordered to create long-context inputs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Datasets were standardized into a unified format for automatic evaluation; public data were extracted from test sets to avoid test leakage; for long-context evaluation, complete Wikipedia passages containing supporting/distracting paragraphs were used as context, and DuReader questions were paired with related documents plus distractors up to 20 documents.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We employ two extraction strategies: random sampling and uniform sampling. ... Initially, supporting passages are included within the context, and then as many distracting passages are added until the total length reaches a maximum length. Finally, these passages are randomly ordered to form the multi-document context.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: All datasets in LongBench are standardized into a unified format, allowing for effortless automatic evaluation of LLMs. ... to avoid test leakage, we extract data from the test sets of these public datasets ... To tailor the data for long-context evaluation, we utilize complete Wikipedia passages encompassing the supporting or distracting paragraphs as the context. ... for each question, we not only provide several documents related to the question but also arbitrarily select several from the total set of documents as distractors, until each question is associated with 20 documents.
